Let Y be a fresh independent fair bit and F=G+Y sum C_j(u_j-G), retaining ONE actual G on both children. If G is an exclusive selector of disjoint independent cores with Z=sum a_l Var(g_l), define the original physically merged fine selector reserve R=sum eta(q_label)Var(core_label), kappa=R-E R_child, m_j=E u_j, n=E G, V=1-n^2, h=sum C_j(m_j-n), h0=E h, and k_t=eta(1-t/2)-eta(1-t)/2. Then kappa=sum p_j Var(u_j)/2+k_t Z, actual queried influence d=sum p_j(1-m_j n)/2, and B_Y-kappa=Var(h)/2+Phi((n+h0/2)^2,(h0/2)^2)+[t(1-t)/2+Phi((1-t/2)^2,(t/2)^2)]V-k_t Z<=8d. Consequently D_Y H-kappa<=(8+2/ln2)d, with all biases, constants and t endpoints allowed, after every actual preceding restriction preserving this decomposition. For a private point-priority prefix and disjoint private point-priority fallback, arbitrary DATA-only histories followed by Y and arbitrary private controller/data continuation obey the same stopped fine U/R theorem as accepted A059 v2 at Kctrl=6+(5+ln10)/ln2<17, retaining actual unresolved H-U-R and resolved boundary<=I_leaf/ln2. Private controller queries before Y and arbitrary inherited U are not paid by this claim.
